message.content:
`docker start` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker daemon itself.  
To bring the Docker Engine (or Docker Desktop) up on Windows you need to start the underlying service:

```powershell
# PowerShell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

or, if you prefer the classic command prompt:

```cmd
net start com.docker.service
```

Once the `com.docker.service` is running, the Docker CLI (`docker`) will be able to communicate with the daemon. If you’re using Docker Desktop, you can also just launch the Docker Desktop app from the Start menu – it automatically starts the service for you.
